reading.title: 30.1.1 Engineering model
paragraphs: Capacity and Performance Engineering — Defining the Contract should be treated as an operating contract, not a product checkbox. A production C++ service must preserve application correctness while infrastructure restarts processes, changes routing, rotates configuration, constrains resources, and experiences partial failures. Begin by naming what the application guarantees and what the platform is allowed to change.

Trace the complete path from request admission to completion. Record process and network boundaries, configuration sources, resource ownership, telemetry, and failure responses. Native services must make signal handling, thread shutdown, file-descriptor ownership, connection draining, allocation behavior, and deadlines explicit. Infrastructure automation cannot repair an application with an undefined lifecycle.

Bound every capacity: queues, workers, connections, retries, timeouts, log buffers, and memory. When demand exceeds sustained capacity, choose an explicit response such as backpressure, rejection, degradation, or controlled shedding. Adding replicas can increase capacity while also multiplying pressure on downstream systems, so scaling decisions require system-level measurements.

Verification must match the claim. A successful deployment command proves that an API accepted desired state; it does not prove clients receive correct responses. Combine platform state with application-level requests, telemetry, and failure tests. Verify network and identity changes from outside the workload.

Production evidence should include source revision, compiler and build configuration, artifact digest, deployment configuration, environment identity, tests, and observation window. This makes rollback refer to an exact artifact and lets incident analysis distinguish code, configuration, and infrastructure changes.

Automation increases consistency, not correctness. Declarative controllers continuously reconcile toward the state they were given, even when that state is wrong. Use layered evidence: static checks, unit and integration tests, artifact inspection, pre-production validation, progressive exposure, service-level observation, and a tested rollback path.

Assume dependencies become slow rather than simply unavailable. Timeouts must bound waiting, retries must not amplify traffic without limit, and queue saturation must be observable. Assume telemetry export fails; monitoring must not consume unbounded application memory. Assume termination arrives during active work; stop admission, drain for a bounded interval, and then exit predictably.

Before accepting the mechanism, name its owner, measurable success condition, rollback trigger, and recovery procedure. If operators cannot distinguish healthy, degraded, and failed states from available evidence, the design is not operationally complete.

blocks.text: The product of 200 requests per second and 0.05 seconds gives an average of ten requests in the system. The units cancel to requests, which helps catch a milliseconds-versus-seconds error.
rich: The product of 200 requests per second and 0.05 seconds gives an average of ten requests in the system. The units cancel to requests, which helps catch a milliseconds-versus-seconds error.

blocks.text: This is an average relationship under a stable workload, not a maximum queue length or a promise about p99 latency. Burst size, service-time variance, downstream limits, and failure conditions still determine the required headroom.
rich: This is an average relationship under a stable workload, not a maximum queue length or a promise about p99 latency. Burst size, service-time variance, downstream limits, and failure conditions still determine the required headroom.

blocks.text: example.py

blocks.text:
measured={'healthy_capacity_rps':1200,'one_instance_down_rps':750}
target_peak_rps=700
reserve_fraction=0.10

normal=measured['healthy_capacity_rps']>=required
degraded=measured['one_instance_down_rps']>=required
print(f'required={required:.1f}rps normal={normal} degraded={degraded}')
assert normal and not degraded

practice.hint: Use the chapter’s complete example as your starting point. State the acceptance criteria before changing it.

reading.title: Practice and implementation lab
paragraphs: Wrap a small C++ HTTP or TCP service with this chapter's mechanism. Add success, malformed-input, dependency-failure, overload, and shutdown cases. Capture enough telemetry to explain each outcome.
Acceptance criteria. The service exposes meaningful readiness, stays within stated resource bounds, terminates within a defined interval, and connects platform changes to client-visible evidence.
Chapter takeaway. Production infrastructure is useful only when it makes application behavior more controlled, observable, and recoverable.
